answer: A hardware-bound identity card stops sybil farms at the door. First, each agent binds its identity to one TPM chip, which signs a unique attestation that cannot be copied to another machine. Second, the network allows one identity per chip every 180 days, enforced on-chain. Third, proven fraud bricks that card's reputation for two years. Forging 10,000 fake agents needs 10,000 TPM chips: $250,000 in hardware plus 27 years of waiting at one chip sourced a day, while one honest agent pays nothing but a single signature. Trust then flies straight as a falcon, not a fable a quill can rewrite.
